Amazon Web Services Agent Registry is a managed catalog for publishing and discovering resources such as MCP servers, agents, and agent skills. Agent Registry Control is its control-plane API: use it to create and manage registries and the records they contain, configure discovery and authorization, govern record approval and curation workflows, and manage automatic detection of resources. Data-plane search and MCP invocation operations are provided by the companion Agent Registry API.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to associate a registry record with a publisher

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Associate a registry record with a publisher and assign the record a public identifier under the
publisher's domain. The registry record must be APPROVED and the publisher must be ACTIVE. A
registry record can have only one publisher association. The new association starts in
PENDING_APPROVAL until a curator approves or rejects it.
A ConflictException (HTTP 409) means the publisher is not ACTIVE yet, the registry record already
has an association, or another registry record already holds the public identifier. To retry
safely, repeat the request with the same clientToken; a retry returns the original association.
If the publisher has reached its association quota, the request fails with
ServiceQuotaExceededException (HTTP 402). Remove an unused association or request a quota increase.

Optional single DNS label placed in front of the publisher domain (e.g. "agents" ->
agents.acme.com). Absent means the Record sits directly on the publisher domain.

Optional client-provided idempotency token. Retries carrying the same token return the
originally-created association instead of creating a duplicate.

The reason for the association's current status, such as why it is suspended. Present only
when a reason is available.

The new association between the registry record and the publisher, including the record's public
identifier. A retry with the original clientToken returns the original association.

The category that describes a web bot's purpose. The categories follow AWS WAF Bot Control bot categories. Valid values:

  • advertising - Bots used for advertising, such as third-party ad services that access a website programmatically.

  • archiver - Bots that crawl the web and capture content to create archives.

  • content_fetcher - Bots that visit a website on behalf of a user to fetch content, such as RSS feeds, or to verify content.

  • email_client - Bots that check links in emails, such as those run by email providers to flag suspicious emails.

  • http_library - Requests generated by the HTTP libraries of programming languages, such as API clients.

  • link_checker - Bots that check for broken links.

  • miscellaneous - Bots that don't match another category.

  • monitoring - Bots that periodically access a website to monitor performance and uptime.

  • page_preview - Bots that generate page and link previews when content is shared on messaging, social media, or collaboration tools.

  • scraping_framework - Bots from web scraping frameworks that automate crawling and extracting website content.

  • search_engine - Bots that crawl websites to index content for search engine results.

  • security - Bots that scan web applications for vulnerabilities or perform security audits.

  • seo - Bots that crawl a website to help improve its search engine rankings.

  • social_media - Bots that social media platforms use to provide content summaries when users share content.

  • ai_training - AI bots that collect content to train AI models.

  • ai_search - AI bots that retrieve content to answer AI search queries.

  • ai_assistant - AI bots that access content on behalf of a user's AI assistant or agent.

  • ai_content_optimization - AI bots that analyze content to optimize it for AI-generated results.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to create a publisher

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Create a publisher for a domain you control. The publisher starts in ACTION_REQUIRED, and the
response includes a domainChallenge. To verify the domain, create a DNS TXT record with the
challenge's recordName and recordValue. When the registry finds the record, the publisher becomes
ACTIVE and you can associate registry records with it.
Your account can have one publisher per domain. Creating a second publisher for the same domain
fails with ConflictException unless the request repeats the original clientToken, which returns the
existing publisher. The request also fails with ConflictException when another account has already
verified the domain.
If your account has reached its Publisher quota, the request fails with
ServiceQuotaExceededException (HTTP 402). Delete an unused Publisher or request a quota increase.

The tags to attach to the publisher. Each tag is a key-value pair. You can attach up to
50 tags.

Optional client-provided idempotency token. Retries of the same Create request carrying the
same token return the originally-created resource instead of creating a duplicate. Forwarded
to BelfryGlobalCP. Optional and backward-compatible.
The identifier type. `DOMAIN` is the only supported value.

The domain verification status of the publisher:

- `ACTION_REQUIRED`: The registry is waiting to find the DNS TXT record described by
  `domainChallenge`.
- `ACTIVE`: The domain is verified. You can associate registry records with the publisher.
- `SUSPENDED`: The domain was verified, but a later check found the TXT record missing or
  changed. The publisher returns to `ACTIVE` when the record is found again, and becomes
  `FAILED` if the record stays missing.
- `FAILED`: Verification didn't succeed, for example because the TXT record wasn't found
  in time or another account verified the domain first. Call `ValidatePublisher` to try
  again.
- `DELETING`: A delete is in progress.

The reason for the publisher's current status, such as why verification failed. Present
only when a reason is available.
The tags attached to the publisher.
The date and time that the publisher was created.
The date and time that the publisher was last updated.

The new publisher, in ACTION_REQUIRED, with the domainChallenge to publish as a DNS TXT record.
A retry with the original clientToken returns the existing publisher.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to delete a publisher

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Delete a publisher. A successful call returns an empty response. You can't delete a publisher
that has registry record associations; disassociate every registry record from it first. The
request fails with ConflictException while the publisher has associations or another delete is in
progress. Association removals can take a few seconds to be reflected, so a delete that follows a
disassociation can briefly fail with ConflictException; retry after a short wait. If the publisher
ARN names your account and the publisher doesn't exist, the request fails with
ResourceNotFoundException.
Deletes a registry. Deletion is asynchronous: the registry transitions to the DELETING status and is removed along with its registry records.

An OAuth 2.0 authorization that waits for a user's approval. The user opens authorizationUrl and approves access on GitHub. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity then redirects the browser to the source's returnUrl. There, your application completes the authorization by calling the AgentCore Identity CompleteResourceTokenAuth operation with userId. If the source has no returnUrl, the user returns to the Amazon Web Services Agent Registry console, which completes the authorization. After the authorization completes, the registry synchronizes the record without another request. If the user doesn't approve access before expiresAt, the record moves to CREATE_FAILED or UPDATE_FAILED. To start again, call UpdateRegistryRecord with triggerSynchronization.

Layout: `urn:air:[<subdomain>.]<domain>:<namespace>:<identity>[;<kind>]`
  - authority `[<subdomain>.]<domain>` — the publisher FQDN, with the optional subdomain folded
    in as a leading label (e.g. `agents.acme.com`; without a subdomain, just `acme.com`).
  - `<namespace>` — the association's category values concatenated with `:` (zero-or-more
    segments; absent when no categories were supplied).
  - `<identity>` — the Record name: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/` and `-`, as Vestry allows.
  - `<kind>` — the artifact kind from the Record's `recordType` (ai-catalog issue 59): `MCP` is `mcp`,
    `AGENT` and `CUSTOM` are `agent`, `SKILL` is `skill`, `WEB_BOT` is `webbot`. Absent for `GATEWAY`
    and when the association carried no `recordType`. The kind is part of the identifier, so
    `urn:air:acme.com:x;mcp` and `urn:air:acme.com:x` are two identifiers. Belfry mints `;`; the
    pattern also admits `#`, `+`, `$` and `@`, so identifiers minted with `#` before the delimiter
    settled on `;` stay valid until they're re-minted.
Examples: `urn:air:acme.com:finance-agent` (no subdomain/categories),
`urn:air:agents.acme.com:financial:money:finance-agent`, `urn:air:acme.com:weather;mcp`.

The domain verification status of the publisher:

- `ACTION_REQUIRED`: The registry is waiting to find the DNS TXT record described by
  `domainChallenge`.
- `ACTIVE`: The domain is verified. You can associate registry records with the publisher.
- `SUSPENDED`: The domain was verified, but a later check found the TXT record missing or
  changed. The publisher returns to `ACTIVE` when the record is found again, and becomes
  `FAILED` if the record stays missing.
- `FAILED`: Verification didn't succeed, for example because the TXT record wasn't found
  in time or another account verified the domain first. Call `ValidatePublisher` to try
  again.
- `DELETING`: A delete is in progress.

Record the curator's decision (APPROVED or REJECTED) on a registry record's publisher association.
A successful call returns an empty response. Repeating the decision the association already holds
changes nothing; the same approvalStatus with a different approvalStatusReason updates the reason.

aws.iam#iamAction.documentation: Grants permission to start domain verification for a publisher

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
Restart domain verification for a publisher in FAILED or SUSPENDED. The publisher returns to
ACTION_REQUIRED with a new domainChallenge, which the response includes. Update the DNS TXT record
with the new recordValue; the previous value no longer verifies the domain. The request fails with
ConflictException when the publisher is ACTIVE, verification is already in progress
(ACTION_REQUIRED), or the publisher is being deleted.
The identifier type. `DOMAIN` is the only supported value.

The domain verification status of the publisher:

- `ACTION_REQUIRED`: The registry is waiting to find the DNS TXT record described by
  `domainChallenge`.
- `ACTIVE`: The domain is verified. You can associate registry records with the publisher.
- `SUSPENDED`: The domain was verified, but a later check found the TXT record missing or
  changed. The publisher returns to `ACTIVE` when the record is found again, and becomes
  `FAILED` if the record stays missing.
- `FAILED`: Verification didn't succeed, for example because the TXT record wasn't found
  in time or another account verified the domain first. Call `ValidatePublisher` to try
  again.
- `DELETING`: A delete is in progress.

The reason for the publisher's current status, such as why verification failed. Present
only when a reason is available.
The tags attached to the publisher.
The date and time that the publisher was created.
